name: Echinacea

project_scope.note: Single-species genus study lesson uses identified neighboring taxa as references, not learner-approved new species. No new canonical species or nativity changes.

genus_recognition.look_here_first: Look for a compact, often single-headed coneflower with *narrow rough leaves*, stiff cone and papery/prickly receptacular chaff between disk florets. The purple rays are WHOLE RAY FLORETS, not petals.
genus_recognition.source_order: habit → leaf/stem architecture → flower structure → fruit/seed → specialist comparison

morphological_comparison_matrix.comparison_reference: purpurea generally larger/branched; pallida taller/slender; Ratibida often slender branching

morphological_comparison_matrix.Echinacea angustifolia: narrow linear to lanceolate, hairy/rough and mostly entire
morphological_comparison_matrix.comparison_reference: purpurea often broad toothed ovate leaves; pallida also narrow so other traits required

morphological_comparison_matrix.Echinacea angustifolia: shorter broad stiff prickly cone built of disk florets plus paleae/chaff
morphological_comparison_matrix.comparison_reference: Ratibida columnifera has dramatically elongated column-shaped disk

morphological_comparison_matrix.Echinacea angustifolia: pink-purple drooping rays, often relatively short compared with E. pallida
morphological_comparison_matrix.comparison_reference: pallida often has very narrow long strongly drooping rays; color not diagnostic

morphological_comparison_matrix.Echinacea angustifolia: usually narrow basal/cauline leaves, not deeply divided
morphological_comparison_matrix.comparison_reference: Ratibida has conspicuously deeply divided/lobed leaves

morphological_comparison_matrix.Echinacea angustifolia: achenes (cypselae) with reduced pappus; image should show scale and phyllaries
morphological_comparison_matrix.comparison_reference: compare with Ratibida and other Asteraceae; dry fruit alone not sufficient

visual_id_sequence: 1. Inspect entire plant habit and growth form.
2. Zoom to stem node and complete mature leaf with ruler.
3. Inspect close flower and reproductive parts, labeling all structures rather than flower color alone.
4. Confirm mature fruit architecture with macro and seed view.
5. Compare the nearest confuser against matched structural photos; keep ambiguous IDs at genus.

diagnostic_photo_requirements.show: entire leaf with mm/cm ruler and hairs, upper/lower surfaces
full habit with branched stem or single head, basal leaves
head side view showing shape/height of disk and rays
E. angustifolia vs pallida narrow rays and leaves and purpurea broad leaves same scale

scientific_cautions: Pallida overlap requires flower-ray dimensions and involucral phyllaries matched image; maintain source-pool E. angustifolia's canonical native_target_zone_calculated=false.
A canonical species's current target-zone nativity and learner approval are scientific metadata; comparing other related taxa must not install them or change their statuses.
Flower color, single leaf and ecology alone never resolve difficult look-alikes; photo comparisons should show same scale and source provenance.
